title: Nasdaq-100 constituents + weights (market_data/index_constituents/NDX.json, v1)
description: Producer: collectors/nasdaq100.py::collect (alpha-engine-config-I11296). Membership from Nasdaq's own published list; per-constituent weight computed from the fleet's licensed fundamentals market-cap archive rather than a scraped cap string. Consumer: collectors/index_contributions.py (D48, alpha-engine-config-I11297), which reads weight_map for the NDX leg of the per-constituent contribution decomposition. Written to market_data/index_constituents/NDX.json (latest) and market_data/weekly/{date}/NDX.json (point-in-time), identical bodies. Sibling to constituents.json, which covers the S&P indices; historical_constituents.py's S&P replay is untouched by this file. UNITS: weight_map values are FRACTIONS normalised to sum 1.0 over the WEIGHTED SUBSET (not over all members) -- see weight_map and unweighted_tickers, which must be read together.

tickers.description: Published membership. 101 securities, not 100: the Nasdaq-100 holds 100 companies but 101 securities because of a dual share class. A consumer hard-coding 100 fails on that pair, which is why the producer raises outside [100, 102] rather than trimming.

index_of.description: The index each weighted ticker belongs to. Constant here, and present so a consumer can treat this artifact and constituents.json through one shape rather than special-casing per file.

weight_map.description: Per-constituent index weight as FRACTIONS summing to 1.0 over the WEIGHTED SUBSET — the members for which a market cap was available — NOT over all members. A member absent from this map is in unweighted_tickers and has UNKNOWN weight, never zero weight. Reading weight_map alone therefore overstates each weight by the reciprocal of coverage; a consumer that cares must check weighted_count against constituent_count.

raw_sum.description: Pre-normalisation weight sum in the source's own units. The only place a units flip or a coverage collapse stays visible: normalisation would otherwise absorb it and the weights would still sum to 1.0 while being wrong.

weight_method.description: Which rung of the source ladder actually produced these weights, and therefore how much to trust them. 'modified_cap_approx' means the Nasdaq-100's MODIFIED market-cap weighting — annual reconstitution plus special rebalances that cap the mega-caps — was approximated by plain cap weighting, so the error is real and bounded but not zero. 'cache_no_weights' means none are present. This value must reach every downstream consumer unchanged: an approximation that does not travel with its data gets absorbed as fact.

weighted_count.description: Members that got a weight. Compare against constituent_count for coverage — equality is the only case in which weight_map describes the whole index.

unweighted_tickers.description: Members with no market cap available, and therefore no weight. Named rather than silently dropped: an absent weight is unknown, and a consumer reading it as zero would drop a real constituent's contribution while still appearing to reconcile.

market_cap_source.description: The archive key the market caps came from, so a weight can be traced to the snapshot that produced it.

invesco_status.description: Outcome of rung 1, the fund-issuer holdings file that is the direct analogue of the SSGA source trusted for the S&P indices. MEASURED 2026-09-21: 'unavailable_406' — the Invesco host refuses this client on every path tried, including the plain HTML product pages, which is host-level bot protection rather than a wrong URL. Recorded in the payload so the fallback is visible in the data and not only in a commit message; if this ever reads OK, weights stop being an approximation.

fetched_at.description: Wall-clock stamp of the fetch, not a data value (alpha-engine-config-I10894): shadow/parity.py excludes it from `values.breaches` and reports it under `provenance_diffs`, because a shadow run and its live counterpart never fetch at the same instant.
